airport.name: Sierra Vista Municipal Airport / Libby Army Air Field

summary: Sierra Vista Municipal Airport / Libby Army Air Field (FHU) is a joint-use military-civilian airport located on Fort Huachuca, a U.S. Army installation in southeastern Arizona. The facility supports both U.S. Army aviation operations and general aviation, serving the nearby city of Sierra Vista and surrounding Cochise County. It also plays a key role supporting the fort's intelligence, electronic testing, and unmanned aircraft system training missions.
faqs:
Q: Is Sierra Vista Municipal Airport open to civilian travelers?
A: Yes, while the airfield shares runways with Libby Army Air Field on Fort Huachuca, the airport accommodates civilian general aviation and some commercial charter operations.

Q: What military units are based at Libby Army Air Field?
A: The airfield has historically supported Army aviation, intelligence training, and unmanned aircraft programs associated with Fort Huachuca's missions.

Q: Why do I need ID or base access to fly into FHU?
A: Because the airport sits within Fort Huachuca, civilian visitors must pass through a security gate and may need to coordinate base access in advance.

Q: Are there scheduled commercial flights to FHU?
A: Commercial service is very limited; most travelers use Tucson International Airport about 70 miles northwest for scheduled flights.
transport_tips: Ground transportation options include rental cars, taxi services, and rideshares, though availability can be limited—booking in advance is recommended. Visitors without military ID must stop at the Fort Huachuca visitor center at the main gate to obtain a day pass before proceeding to the airfield. The drive from Tucson International Airport takes roughly 1.5 hours via I-10 and SR-90.
local_tip: Carry a valid photo ID and your flight itinerary at all times—Fort Huachuca security checkpoints are active 24/7 and civilian drivers can be turned away without proper documentation, even for airport pickup or drop-off.
